name: Maximal Area Quadrilateral
description: Iahub has drawn a set of n points in the cartesian plane which he calls "special points". A quadrilateral is a simple polygon without self-intersections with four sides (also called edges) and four vertices (also called corners). Please note that a quadrilateral doesn't have to be convex. A special quadrilateral is one which has all four vertices in the set of special points. Given the set of special points, please calculate the maximal area of a special quadrilateral.
input_specification: The first line contains integer n ( 4 ≤ n ≤ 300 ). Each of the next n lines contains two integers: x i , y i ( - 1000 ≤ x i , y i ≤ 1000) — the cartesian coordinates of i th special point. It is guaranteed that no three points are on the same line. It is guaranteed that no two points coincide.
output_specification: Output a single real number — the maximal area of a special quadrilateral. The answer will be considered correct if its absolute or relative error does't exceed 10 - 9 .
